d: Historic interplanetary landing sites, sample return bodies, and planetary exploration landmarks.

venus.x: First planetary atmosphere probed (Venera 4) and first robotic surface landing on another world (Venera 7 in 1970).

moon.x: Site of six crewed Apollo lunar landings (1969–1972) and numerous robotic sample-return missions.

mars.x: Planetary surface explored by Viking, Pathfinder, Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity, and Perseverance searching for ancient biosignatures.

433-eros.x: First asteroid orbited and landed upon by a spacecraft (NEAR Shoemaker in February 2001).

101955-bennu.x: Carbonaceous near-Earth asteroid sampled by NASA’s OSIRIS-REx mission in 2020, delivering pristine primordial material to Earth.

162173-ryugu.x: Primitive C-type asteroid sampled by JAXA’s Hayabusa2 spacecraft in 2018–2019, returning sub-surface organics and amino acids.

67p-churyumov.x: Jupiter-family comet orbited by ESA’s Rosetta spacecraft and touched down upon by the Philae lander in November 2014.

titan.x: Site of ESA’s Huygens probe landing in January 2005, the most distant landing ever conducted in the Solar System.

b.s: Historic landing and sample return locations marking human and robotic exploration milestones across the Solar System.
